findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring offsets
findings.body: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the token when the shortcut matches, so it accepts wrong grants and rejects correct ones. The comment and offsets are also wrong. The context prefix is 6 chars with the grant at indices 4..6, so substring(3,5) takes the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant. Tests using expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh and similar will fail, or if they pass they verify nothing.

findings.title: requireNonNull checks grantType twice, rawTokenId never checked
findings.body: The fourth check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`. It should check rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId is accepted and produces a token id ending in 'null'.

findings.title: Token creation throws for flows that don't set GRANT_TYPE
findings.body: initToken now always calls encodeTokenId. If the GRANT_TYPE attribute is not set on the client session context, the grant falls back to "na". Unknown grant types are mapped ("na" is in the map), so that case still encodes. But a custom grant type factory that is not registered, or a flow that sets a grant id lacking a shortcut, makes encodeTokenId throw IllegalStateException. Other token-creation paths (implicit/hybrid flow, token-exchange legacy providers, admin or account flows) never set GRANT_TYPE and now get an 'na' encoding. That differs from the documented design and may break consumers expecting a UUID.

findings.title: Lightweight detection depends on the session's current client
findings.body: getShouldUseLightweightToken(session) reads session.getContext().getClient(), which may be null or differ from the client the token is issued for, for example during refresh or token exchange. It can throw an NPE or encode the wrong token type.

findings.title: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws on any ID containing ':' that isn't 6-char prefixed
findings.body: Any token id with a ':' whose prefix is not exactly 6 characters throws IllegalArgumentException. This includes old or foreign ids, which would break callers that parse arbitrary tokens.
